requirements.text: The assigned resource, Thomas Green, is showing as inactive in the system; immediately activate him
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 1 AND first_name = 'Thomas' AND last_name = 'Green' AND email = 'thomas.green@servicenow.com' AND active = 1 AND role = 'agent'
assumptions: Thomas Green is user 1 (thomas.green@servicenow.com), the only user of that name, inactive on the seed
name, email and role are seed facts kept from the benchmark check; role agent lets him be assigned the case

requirements.text: assign him to handle this case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 783 AND state = 'in_progress' AND assigned_to = 1 AND assignment_group_id = 1 AND priority = 'critical' AND account_id = 34 AND contact_id = 73 AND product_id = 35
assumptions: case CS-0000783 is case_id 783 (pending, critical, assigned to user 328, group 1 CSM Tier 1 Support; contact 73 is Ashley Krueger)

state in_progress kept from the benchmark check; implied by the request, not stated: the pending case is to be handled and its resolution SLA attached, the policy aligns an SLA when a case moves to work in progress, and pending to in_progress is a valid transition
assignment_group_id 1 is the case's group on the seed and the group he joins; kept from the benchmark check
priority, account 34 (Estrada LLC), contact 73 and product 35 (Docker Enterprise Variant 15) are seed facts kept from the benchmark check
the case number is server-kept and is not a cell; case_id 783 carries it

requirements.text: Make sure he's added to the right assignment group if needed
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE group_id = 1 AND user_id = 1
assumptions: the policy requires the assignee to be a member of the case's assignment group; user 1 belongs to no group on the seed, so membership in group 1 is needed
two memberships are created in this task in no fixed order, so the row is selected by group and user, not by member_id

requirements.text: then attach the appropriate resolution SLA to it
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_sla_id = 2465 AND case_id = 783 AND sla_def_id = 6
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (case_sla_id 2465 after 2464)
the appropriate resolution SLA for a critical case is sla_def_id 6 (SLA Resolution - Critical, metric resolution, active)
stage, start and breach times are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested

requirements.text: document this reassignment with an interaction record so we have an audit trail
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM interaction WHERE interaction_id = 1233 AND case_id = 783
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (interaction_id 1233 after 1232)
channel, status, account, contact and interacted user are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested

requirements.text: Please adjust the default Critical Resolution SLA target time to 360 minutes
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sla_definition WHERE sla_def_id = 6 AND name = 'SLA Resolution - Critical' AND metric = 'resolution' AND target_mins = 360 AND applies_to_priority = 'critical' AND pause_on_pending = 1 AND active = 1
assumptions: the default Critical Resolution SLA is sla_def_id 6, the only active resolution SLA for critical priority (240 minutes on the seed)
name, metric, priority, pause_on_pending and active are seed facts kept from the benchmark check

requirements.text: adjust the default Critical Resolution SLA target time to 360 minutes
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sla_definition WHERE sla_def_id = 1 AND target_mins = 15
assumptions: boundary of the description: SLA Response - Critical (1) is the near match on name and priority to 'Critical Resolution SLA'; only the resolution SLA changes

requirements.text: establish a new Security Policy Review support team
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group WHERE group_id = 81 AND name = 'Security Policy Review' AND type = 'support' AND active = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (group_id 81 after 80)
active 1 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: add a new cloud security agent named Lisa Casey with email lisa.casey@servicenow.com
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user WHERE user_id = 803 AND first_name = 'Lisa' AND last_name = 'Casey' AND email = 'lisa.casey@servicenow.com' AND active = 1 AND role = 'agent'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (user_id 803 after 802)
role agent from 'agent' in the request
active 1 kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: add ... Lisa Casey ... to this team
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE group_id = 81 AND user_id = 803
assumptions: two memberships are created in this task in no fixed order, so the row is selected by group and user, not by member_id

requirements.text: the Advanced Security Module which should also be added to our product catalog as a new software
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM product WHERE product_id = 241 AND name = 'Advanced Security Module' AND category = 'software' AND lifecycle_state = 'active'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (product_id 241 after 240)
category software from the request
lifecycle_state active kept from the benchmark check; the policy requires products in use to be active
price not stated and not tested

membership_changes.evidence: the task creates two memberships (Thomas Green in group 1, Lisa Casey in group 81) and the request fixes no order between them, so member_id 960 and 961 cannot be tied to particular rows; each membership is selected by group and user instead

notes:
The acting user is a manager; the policy's general instruction has the assistant act with an administrator's responsibilities, so the user, group, membership, SLA definition and product changes are in scope.
'all_changes' is a sum over cells the other checks test and is carried jointly by those requirements; its membership part counts member_id 960 and 961, which holds when the two memberships are the only ones created.
On the seed the case is assigned to Bryan Johnson (user 328), not Thomas Green as the request says; the request's instruction to assign Thomas Green decides the final assignee.
The case already has a paused resolution SLA row (case_sla 1566, definition 6); the request asks for the SLA to be attached, so a new case_sla row is required.
The case_changes check also tests number = 'CS-0000783'; number is a server-kept column restating the anchor, so it is not a cell.
The interaction's channel and participant are not fixed by the request or policy and are left untested.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that SLA Response - Critical (1) keeps its 15-minute target: one pass wrote it, the other did not; kept because it is the near match on name and priority to 'the default Critical Resolution SLA', and the critical case is also linked to it, so a loose reading of the description would change it; that is the selector boundary a stay records.
